results.title: Nuit et Brouillard = Night and Fog
results.brief_description:
“‘Nuit et Brouillard’ establishes the classic photographic dichotomy of the Holocaust film, according to which the past is seen in black and white and the present in colour. The aesthetic quality of the film stems from the inter-relation of Cayrol’s text and Eisler’s music with Resnais’s editing, which juxtaposes colour images of the ruins of the death camps with black and white archive footage of the camps and their victims during the war. Resnais thus excavates the horrors lying beneath the deceptively banal landscapes of the present day, landscapes which like those of Lanzman’s ‘Shoah’ are at times startingly beautiful with blue or pink skies and orange trees. It has even been remarked that these colours were too bright, like open wound or ‘draining blood’. The disembodied and anonymous narration in ‘Nuit et Brouillard’, the film’s universal concerns, and the absence of any reference to the extermination of the Jews might be taken as conforming to the myth of ‘resistancialisme’. Although a specifically French context is given by brief allusions to the camps at Pithiviers and Compiegne, and to the deportation of Jews from the Velodrome d’Hiver in Paris, the image which most explicitly challenge the Gaullist myth - a French policeman surveying the camps at Pithiviers - was censored.” Reference: Guy Austin. ‘Contemporary French Cinema’. Manchester University Press, 1996.

Credits: Producer, Anatole Dauman ; director, Alain Resnais ; photography, Sacha Vierny, Ghislain Cloquet ; music, Hans Eisler ; editor, Henri Colpi.

results.title: New Wave: French Connection
results.brief_description:
A documentary account of a Punk/New Wave festival held in the Fourvieres roman theatre of Lyons in the summer of 1978. Fourvieres made its mark in the history of entertainement as a place where Christians were thrown to the lions. In 1978 only great expectations are shattered as ‘Marie et les garcons’ are booed off the stage. The concert showcases French exponents of the New Wave movement, such as Telephone, Bijou, Starshooters as well as Heavy Metal band Ganafoul and reggae outfit Cimarons, all working hard to prove that there is a world of peaceful harmony outside Disco. The documentary ends with that also familiar concert ritual: an ocean of empty beer cans being swept away.
Cast: Interviews by Jean-Francois Bizot.

results.title: Jean Cocteau: Autoportrait D'un Inconnu
results.brief_description:
In this ‘first person’ documentary, Edgardo Cozarinsky uses a long interview with Cocteau who recounts the intellectual life in Paris at the turn of the XXth Century, as well that the birth of the ‘Avant-guarde’ movement with ‘Les ballet Russes’ and the uproar that accompanied the staging of ‘Parade’.

Credits: Producer, Carole Weisweiller ; director, Edgardo Cozarinsky ; writers, Edgardo Cozarinsky, Carole Weisweiller.

results.title: Monsieur Bais
results.brief_description:
Charles Bais is a well-to-do architect married to Marthe, a harpsicord player. The day following Charles’ purchase of a handgun, Marthe is found dead in bed with a bullet wound to the heart. The murder investigation conducted by Judge Massot reveals that Charles used to enjoy a rather ecclectic sex life and that he was in the habit of sharing his mistresses with his good friend Docteur Noel. Judge Massot’s attention becomes increasingly drawn to one of Charles’ conquest: the mysterious Camille.

Credits: Producer, Jean Gauthier ; director, Claude Barma ; writer, Pierre Dumayet ; photography, Ghislain Cloquet ; music, W. A. Mozart.
Cast: Simone Signoret, Michel Vitold, Didier Haudepin, Anna Karina, Maurice Ronet, Georges Wilson, Gisele Grimm.

results.title: Le Dossier Francoise Muller = the Francoise Muller Case
results.brief_description:
Following an apparence on a TV show, economist Gerard Plantier is murdered in the underground garage of his appartment building. The only witnesses are his girlfriend, Francoise, and the night watchman. As the investigation progresses, it is revealed that Francoise had a rather shady past and that some of her former acquaintances may have something to do with Gerard’s death. To Judge Massot’s surprise, Francoise is doing her best to attract all the blame for the murder to herself.

Credits: Producer, Jean Gauthier ; director, Edouard Molinaro ; writer, Alphonse Boudard ; photography, Alain Levent ; music, Vladimir Cosma.
Cast: Simone Signoret, Michel Vitold, Jean-Claude Dauphin, Didier Haudepin, Bernard Pivot, Albert Simonin, Nathalie Delon, Jean-Pierre Darras, Andre Pousse, Saddy Rebbot, Katy Amaizo, Germaine Delbat, Andre Lacombe, Henry Rellys.

results.title: Autopsie D'un Temoignage = Autopsy of a Witness
results.brief_description:
Elizabeth Massot has taken time off to move into a new appartment. From her windows, she witnesses a cat burgler breaking into a roof-top flat. Elizabeth and an other witness are taken by the police to give their testimony. Elizabeth’s testimony is that of a cautious woman used to ponder the frailty of human evidence. As such, she closely observes the other witness giving an incredibly detailed description of the burgler while enjoying all the attention: is she a reliable witness or just a bored woman relishing her 15 minutes of fame?

Credits: Producer, Jean Gauthier ; director, Philippe Condroyer ; writers, Philippe Condroyer, Mariette Condroyer ; photography, Jean-Jacques Rochut ; music, Antoine Duhamel.
Cast: Simone Signoret, Didier Haudepin, Jean-Claude Dauphin, Michel Vitold, Marie Dubois, Patrick Bouchitey.

results.brief_description:
A couple running a grocery store is found murdered. The prime suspect is their own son, Jean-Michel, a brilliant student. When Elizabeth Massot meets the young man, she becomes intrigued by the relationship he had with his parents and starts drawing parallels between Jean-Michel’s situation and her own volatile relationship with son Guillaume.

Credits: Producer, Jean Gauthier ; director, Claude Chabrol ; writers, Claude Chabrol, Odile Barsky ; photography, Jean Rabier ; music, Pierre Jansen, Vladimir Cosma.
Cast: Simone Signoret, Didier Haudepin, Jean-Claude Dauphin, Michel Vitold, Bernadette Lafont, Mario David, Benoit Ferreux.

results.title: Un Innocent = an Innocent Man
results.brief_description:
Albert and Monique work in a plush hotel, respectively as night watchman and chambermaid. Monique is having an affair with Bob, the hotel barman. In order to finance their plan to elope to Biarritz and get rid of Albert, they set him up to burgle the room of one of the hotel guest. Albert is caught and the case is assigned to Judge Massot. During an interview with Judge Massot, Albert escapes and runs back home where he barricades himself with his children. As the police starts the siege of the house, Judge Massot decides to step in and talk Albert out of doing an even bigger mistake.

Credits: Producer, Jean Gauthier ; director, Nadine Trintigant ; writers, Patrick Modiano ; photography, William Lubtchansky ; music, Georges Delerue.
Cast: Simone Signoret, Didier Haudepin, Jean-Claude Dauphin, Michel Vitold, Philippe Leotard, Juliet Berto, Etienne Chicot, Maurice Garrel, Pierre Vernier, Francois Perrot, Marie Trintignant.

results.title: Le Feu = the Fire
results.brief_description:
Paul, a childhood friend of Judge Elizabeth Massot is dreaming of transforming his country estate into a bird reserve. Unfortunately, his brother, who co-owns the property, has promised it to a land developper. During a bush fire, Paul’s property is devastated by the flames; the following day, the bulldozers arrive to start work on Paul’s land. Judge Massot who is in charge of establishing the criminal origin of the fires cannot fathom why Paul is refusing to file charges against the fire-bugs.

Credits: Producer, Jean Gauthier ; director, Philippe Condroyer ; writers, Mariette Condroyer, Roger Grenier ; photography, Jean-Jacques Rochut ; music, Antoine Duhamel.
Cast: Simone Signoret, Didier Haudepin, Jean-Calude Dauphin, Maurice Garrel, Francois Perrot, Michel Vitold, Michel Blanc.
